characterization_methods.key_findings: Grain-boundary network decorated by bright κ particles and α particles; lamellar structure of alternating α and γ plates with κ films along interfaces.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe κ-carbide precipitated along grain boundaries and within grains

characterization_methods.key_findings: γ austenite matrix with κ-carbide band along a boundary; intragranular γ, κ plates and γ_twin twins; hexagonal SAED ring (spots 200, 101, 111, 110) confirming κ-carbide.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify γ austenite matrix, κ-carbide bands, twins and intragranular κ plates

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM, Mag = 5.10 kX, WD = 7.0 mm, EHT = 15.00 kV, Signal A = QBSD
characterization_methods.key_findings: Intergranular crack follows a grain boundary decorated by localized strain and micro-voids; strain-localization bands flank the crack in the KAM map.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize hydrogen-induced intergranular cracking in Fe-26Mn-11Al-1.2C austenitic steel containing κ-carbides
characterization_methods.technique: EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) and kernel average misorientation (KAM) mapping plus orientation-optimized ECC imaging

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts steel density from Al, C and Mn mass fractions
analytical_models.model_note: C content plays the most significant role in reducing density; the C solid solution is generally below 1.2 wt% in austenite.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts austenite lattice constant from Al, C and Mn mass fractions
analytical_models.model_note: C (interstitial) expands the austenite lattice constant more than Mn and Al (substitutional).

Relates yield strength increment to Mn content
Relates yield strength increment to C content
analytical_models.model_note: C and Al play a more positive role in yield-strength increment than Mn.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Under plastic deformation the interaction between κ-carbides and dislocations does not change the plane slip mode, but additional dislocation sources are activated and acted upon by cross slip; nano κ-carbides uniformly distributed in austenite promote plane slip, and as strain increases the plane dislocation structure is further refined, contributing to continuous strain hardening.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation pile-up at B2/γ phase boundary
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Compared with κ-carbide, B2 phase is not sheared by slip dislocations, leading to dislocation pile-up at the phase boundary and enhancing work hardening during plastic deformation.

interfaces.interface_notes: The κ'-carbide nucleated within the austenite matrix is ultrafine and shows a coherent relationship with the matrix. The κ-carbide/austenite interface (with vacancies) is considered an effective hydrogen capture center.
interfaces.phase_evolution: When the aging temperature ranges from 500 to 700 °C, spinodal decomposition occurs in austenite: γ → γ' + γ'' → γ'' + L1₂ (short-range ordering phase) + γ' + κ'. At higher aging temperature (700–900 °C) coarse κ'-carbide forms in the austenite matrix or along the prior austenite grain boundary (called intercrystalline κ*-carbide).
interfaces.slip_behavior: In single austenite-base steels, plane slip of dislocations and the shear effect of mobile dislocations on ordered phases dominate; deformation mechanisms (MBIP, DSBR, SIP, TL) depend on stacking fault energy.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: fatigue life relative to a Fe-12Cr-1.5Ni-0.2V-1.8W-0.5Mo-0.15C martensite stainless steel
comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: about twice (≈2×) that of the martensite stainless steel

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: General Fe-Mn-Al-C thermal-mechanical processing: the forging ingot is homogenized at 1100–1250 °C for 1–3 h before hot rolling.

Hot-rolled to 2–5 mm thickness between 1100 and 850 °C; in some cases reheating between rolling passes is needed to avoid crack generation. A large rolling reduction provides enough recrystallization driving force, inhibiting Fe-Al or FeAl segregation. For austenite-base steels the thermal-mechanical processing temperature is generally located within the single austenite phase region.

Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels after hot rolling and rapidly cooling to room temperature classify into single ferrite/austenite, A-BDP and F-BDP steels. For austenite-base steels the hot-rolled steels can be rapidly cooled to room temperature (Route 1). The cooling rate after hot rolling strongly influences intergranular κ-carbide formation.

structures.overall_structure: Room-temperature microstructure of single austenite Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is composed of equiaxed austenite together with annealing twins, because the temperature of thermal-mechanical processing is generally located within the single austenite phase region.

unmapped_findings: For austenite-base Fe-Mn-Al-C steel, 1 wt% C contributes a yield-strength increment of 187–300 MPa, whereas 1 wt% Al contributes slightly below 10 MPa; Mn addition improves the austenite fraction and increases the solubility of Al and C in austenite, indirectly affecting mechanical properties. (b0061)

High C (>0.7 wt%) and Al (>7.0 wt%) contents are the primary conditions for κ-carbide formation in single austenite-base Fe-Mn-Al-C steels; the aging temperature and time should be precisely regulated to avoid intergranular κ*-carbide and β-Mn formation. (b0071)

Representative single-austenite Fe-Mn-Al-C SFE / deformation-mechanism data (Table 3): Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C, SFE 80 mJ·m⁻², DSBR+MBIP, YS/UTS 0.85; Fe-16Mn-2Al-0.45C, SFE 92 mJ·m⁻², TWIP+DSBR, YS/UTS 0.85; Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C, SFE 110 mJ·m⁻², DSBR+MBIP, YS/UTS 0.87; Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C, SFE 120 mJ·m⁻², DSBR+SIP+MBIP, YS/UTS 0.66. (b0096)

Low-density TWIP steels (single austenite) have a high Mn content of 20–30 wt%; after rolling, annealing and quenching the microstructure consists of complete austenite together with a large number of annealing twins. (b0090)

Fe-28Mn-10Al-1.2C steel with SFE of 110 mJ/m² contains austenite, ferrite and κ-carbides; deformation twins are almost restrained and nano κ-carbides are uniformly arranged on the austenitic matrix with a certain spacing, giving the SIP effect. (b0089)

The MBIP mechanism was proposed for quenched Fe-28Mn-xAl-(0.8–1.0)C steel: nano short-range ordering phases precipitate in partial areas, microbands form under high strain, and the interaction among microbands refines grains (873 MPa tensile strength and 100% total elongation via dynamic Hall-Petch effect). (b0091)
Fe-30.4Mn-8Al-1.2C low-density steel with SFE of 85 mJ/m² deforms mainly by dynamic slip band refinement (DSBR), giving 900 MPa tensile strength and 68% total elongation. (b0091)
